text:
anna: Quick follow-up on the verifier agent API question from the RFC — I sketched a minimal boundary for on-prem/package-verifier and wanted feedback.
miguel: sgtm to get a small API surface. what are the trust assumptions? who verifies the signer chain?
anna: assume control plane signs manifests and bundles with org KMS. on-prem verifier validates signature + hash. if offline, verifier must accept an anchor bundle provided via airgap medium.
kevin: sounds right. two immediate choices: (A) tight RPC to control plane to fetch public keys + sig revocation lists, or (B) offline-first where all certs are shipped in bundle and rotated via delta bundles. tradeoffs: A needs outbound connectivity or scheduled cert sync; B increases bundle size and rotation complexity.
priya: for regulated customers often no outbound allowed. so B is mandatory for them. but we should still support A for dedicated setups for ease.
anna: agreed. propose a hybrid: verifier supports both modes. default is online sync when reachable. offline mode falls back to local anchoring with manifest chain validation.
miguel: how do we model revocation in offline mode? we can't call home to check CRLs.
kevin: we can use signed revocation manifests that are distributed as deltas. verifier stores last-seen revocation manifest timestamp/hash and refuses bundles older than that if requested by ops. also policy flag allows accept-legacy for emergency.
priya: operational question: Do we expose the agent API as a filesystem shim (pull files) or an HTTP RPC? I prefer HTTP for idempotency and clear responses.
anna: proposed minimal HTTP interface:

```
POST /verify
{
  "bundle_id": "sha256:...",
  "manifest": "{...}",
  "signatures": ["..."],
  "mode": "online|offline"
}

200 OK {"status":"verified","applied":false}
400/422 errors for malformed
```

kevin: add an endpoint for health and last-sync info: GET /status -> {last_cert_sync, mode, last_revocation_ts, metrics}
miguel: pls ensure the API returns machine-friendly error codes for different failure classes (SIG_INVALID, HASH_MISMATCH, POLICY_REJECT). humans hate vague 500s.
priya: also need an apply flow: POST /apply that will atomically swap component bundles with rollback metadata. must include a dry-run flag.
anna: Agreed — apply should be explicit. We also discussed a disk-first verification: verifier writes bundle to a staging dir, runs verification, then returns results. this avoids streaming parsing complexity for very large model artifacts.
miguel: question on metrics/observability: we should expose counters for verify_success, verify_failure_{sig,hash,policy}, last_verification_duration, last_apply_{success,failure}. prometheus exporter? yes please.
kevin: about RBAC: agent runs as local system service. control plane tokens used only when online. token rotation: support both long-lived offline tokens embedded in initial installer and short-lived ones fetched via sync.
priya: regression test idea: create a small harness that simulates revocation deltas and offline anchor upgrades, run through canary apply -> rollback -> final apply.
anna: action items: @miguel write minimal OpenAPI sketch for POST /verify + /apply + /status, @kevin draft on-disk staging semantics and rollback marker format, @priya create test harness plan. I'll collate into RFC appendix.
deploy-bot: deploy status: none — this is design-only thread. :gear:
miguel: ok i'll ping when openapi PR is up, aiming EOD Friday.
kevin: i'll start on the staging prototype tomorrow, will share snippets in #eng-runtime.
priya: i'll draft the harness and include a few offline customer scenarios.
anna: thanks all. if anyone has objections to hybrid online/offline model, speak up now; otherwise I'll add this to RFC appendix and call it the recommended pattern.
miguel: no objections from my side.
kevin: ok from me.
priya: go for it.
